fills.reason: Searched all app sources and the manifest for getExternalStorage*/getExternalFilesDir/getExternalCacheDir/MediaStore and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE: none present. The app reads files via the Storage Access Framework (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT/GET_CONTENT), and it writes user styles to getDir("user-styles", MODE_PRIVATE), which is internal storage.
Searched src/ for SecretKeySpec, Cipher and other JCA key material: the app does no cryptography, so there are no keys at all.

Clipboard.peek logs the full clipboard text when it matches the email, phone-number or URL patterns, so personal data (emails, phone numbers) goes to logcat. No minification or log stripping is set up in build.gradle, so these Log.d calls stay in release builds.

evidence.detail: Clipboard text matching EMAIL_ADDRESS/PHONE/WEB_URL patterns is written to logcat verbatim.
evidence.quote: Log.d("CLIPBOARD", "Text matched pattern " + p.pattern() + ", not pasting: " + text);

fills.reason: ArticleWebView turns on JavaScript but never calls setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs. With minSdk 23 that setting defaults to false, so the third fail condition isn't met. setAllowContentAccess is left at its default.

JavaScript is on, and setAllowFileAccess is not called (it defaults to true with minSdk 23). However, setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs and setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs are never set and default to false since minSdk is 23 (16 or higher), so the third condition isn't met.
The only text input in the layouts is the dictionary search field (inputType text|textNoSuggestions). It doesn't take passwords, PINs or other sensitive data, and it already turns off suggestions.

FLAG_SECURE is not used anywhere. The screens show offline dictionary articles, bookmarks and lookup history. There is no login, payment or credential screen that the Evaluation would treat as sensitive.
Searched src/ for Notification, NotificationCompat and setContentText, and the manifest for POST_NOTIFICATIONS: the app posts no notifications.
There are no password, PIN or OTP input fields in res/layout or src/. The only input is the dictionary search field.

ArticleWebView enables JS and registers itself as $SLOB. The @JavascriptInterface methods (setStyleTitles, getPreferredStyle, exportStyleSwitcherAs, onStyleSet) only exchange stylesheet titles. Navigation is restricted: shouldOverrideUrlLoading sends every non-localhost URL to an external browser. None of the methods touch sensitive data or actions.
The app has no login, payment, permission-request or security-settings interactions; its UI is dictionary search and article viewing. So the lack of touch filtering doesn't meet the fail condition.

In-app navigation uses explicit intents to ArticleCollectionActivity (ArticleWebView, LookupFragment, BlobDescriptorListFragment, MainActivity). The implicit intents (ACTION_VIEW for the browser, ACTION_SEND through a chooser, ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT, ACTION_GET_CONTENT) all hand off to an external app on purpose.

The only implicit intent with extras is ACTION_SEND carrying an external link URL, sent through Intent.createChooser so the user picks the app. The ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT intent only carries EXTRA_ALLOW_MULTIPLE. Neither carries credentials or personal data.
Searched src/ for PendingIntent: no PendingIntent is created.

ExternalArticleActivity's activity-aliases declare VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filters for http/https *.wikipedia.org and *.wiktionary.org links without android:autoVerify. Application enables them at run time to match installed dictionaries. This is by design, since the app can't verify domains it doesn't own, and the links only open offline lookups, so the impact is low.

evidence.detail: http/https deep link to en.m.wikipedia.org declared without android:autoVerify (same pattern for all wiki aliases).

fills.reason: The manifest declares no custom URL scheme. The only <data> schemes are http and https, and aard2.lookup and colordict.intent.action.SEARCH are intent actions, not schemes.

The root AndroidManifest.xml sets android:allowBackup="true" and declares neither fullBackupContent nor dataExtractionRules, so all app data is backed up: the dictionary list, bookmarks, lookup history, prefs and user styles. Whether lookup history counts as sensitive is for a person to decide.

evidence.detail: Backup enabled with no backup or data-extraction rules.

fills.reason: This test runs a backup and restore on a device. Statically, allowBackup="true" with no exclusion rules (AndroidManifest.xml:20), so a run is needed to see which files are restored.
AndroidManifest.xml (sourceSets.main.manifest.srcFile in build.gradle) declares no <provider> elements.
AndroidManifest.xml declares no <provider> elements, FileProvider included.

Exported activities: MainActivity (the launcher) and ExternalArticleActivity plus its disabled-by-default aliases. ExternalArticleActivity only runs dictionary lookups on a caller-supplied query or a localhost/wiki URI and shows the result on screen. It returns no data to the caller and performs no security-relevant action.
AndroidManifest.xml declares no <service> elements.
AndroidManifest.xml declares no <receiver> elements, and src/ has no registerReceiver call.
